- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 10–20% for short-term (1–7d) and medium (8–14d) horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Model underestimates in high-sentiment periods when price is trending upward; apply upward bias of 5–15% for 1–3d ahead.
- Model overestimates in low-sentiment periods when price is trending downward; apply downward bias of 5–15% for 1–3d ahead.
- For 15–30d horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3d, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2d ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- Avoid extreme outliers (forecast > 3x or < 0.3x recent range) unless sentiment confirms strong trend; cap or floor forecasts to 0.5–2x recent range.
